artist_scope: full contract (Tier 2, the state-branching class (a sitting branch on the tail; the crest scaled by health): geckolib_migration_design.md section 5); the rig is not yet in-game (it lands through the seam in a later slice)
character_sheet: A water-loving four-legged pet lizard: a three-part body with a four-spine ridge down its back, a three-part head crowned by three fanned feathers, four legs of six cubes each sharing one hip pivot, and a three-segment tail (HydroliscModel.java createBodyLayer; 40 parts on a 64x128 sheet). It is passive and tameable with cod - one chance in two per fish (EntityHydrolisc.java:222-232) - then follows its owner (:70), sits and stands on a click (:273-278), breeds (:68), is untamed with a glass block (:247-261) and slowly heals its owner at the cost of its own health (:123-130). It flees monsters (:69), panics when hurt (:72), floats (:67) and bobs up in water (:102-105), seeks the nearest water when hurt or at random and heals in it (:117-121, :133-153); every hit is capped at 10 (:204-207). It never attacks: the attack attribute is 1.0 (:95) and no goal strikes. Read it as a wet, skittish pet: legs paddling with the stride, the tail sweeping, the crest fanning - fast and wide when healthy, slow and small when hurt.

groups.name: gait
groups.amplitude: rests per part 0 / -0.488 / -2.347 / -0.628 / -0.628 / +0.174 rad (parts 1-6 of every leg), then pi x 0.25 = 0.785 rad (45 deg) x the walking speed at 1.3 x 0.65 - still (rests only) below the 0.1 threshold
groups.plain: the four six-part legs swing fore and aft with the stride, every part of a leg together: the left front and right back legs one way, the right front and left back the other
groups.math: a = limbSwingAmount > 0.1 ? cos(ageInTicks * 1.3 * 0.65) * pi * 0.25 * limbSwingAmount : 0; lf*/rb*.xRot = rest + a; rf*/lb*.xRot = rest - a
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 1.3 x 0.65 (wingspeed, HydroliscModel.java:20-21): the natural period is 2 pi / 0.845 = 7.4 ticks

groups.name: tail
groups.amplitude: pi x 0.15 = 0.471 rad, taken x 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 along the chain (7 / 13 / 20 deg); ZERO while sitting (the branch)
groups.plain: the tail sweeps side to side, each segment swinging wider than the one before it, and hangs still while the pet sits
groups.math: s = sitting ? 0 : cos(ageInTicks * 1.0 * 0.65) * pi * 0.15; tail1.yRot = s * 0.25; tail2.yRot = s * 0.5; tail3.yRot = s * 0.75; tail2 and tail3 positions re-derived along the previous segment's angle (5 and 8 units)
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 1.0 x 0.65: the natural period is 2 pi / 0.65 = 9.7 ticks

groups.name: crest_outer
groups.amplitude: -0.9 rad rest (left) / +0.9 (right, mirrored), then pi x 0.2 = 0.628 rad (36 deg) at full health; BOTH the rate and the amplitude are multiplied by the health fraction (half health: 0.244 rad/tick, 18 deg)
groups.plain: the two outer crest feathers fan open and closed in mirror, wide and quick when healthy, slow and shallow as the pet is hurt
groups.math: hf = health / maxHealth; c = cos(ageInTicks * 0.75 * 0.65 * hf) * pi * 0.2 * hf; feather1.yRot = c - 0.9; feather3.yRot = -c + 0.9
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 0.75 x 0.65 x hf: the natural period at full health is 2 pi / 0.4875 = 12.9 ticks

groups.name: crest_centre
groups.amplitude: pi x 0.2 = 0.628 rad (36 deg) at full health, rate and amplitude both x the health fraction
groups.plain: the centre feather wags faster than the outer pair, and slows and shrinks with the pet's health
groups.math: hf = health / maxHealth; feather2.yRot = cos(ageInTicks * 1.25 * 0.65 * hf) * pi * 0.2 * hf
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 1.25 x 0.65 x hf: the natural period at full health is 2 pi / 0.8125 = 7.7 ticks

behaviour: One gait rhythm on the legs (HydroliscModel.java:317-341): above a walking speed of 0.1 the cosine of the age x 1.3 x 0.65 (wingspeed), x pi x 0.25, x the walking speed, is added to every part of the left front and right back legs and subtracted from the right front and left back - a 45-degree swing at full stride every 7.4 ticks, nothing at all when standing (the ternary at :317 gives 0 below the threshold, so the legs snap to their rests).

Each leg is six cubes on one pivot with fixed rest angles (0, -0.488, -2.347, -0.628, -0.628, +0.174 rad: the shoulder, an upper leg, a folded forearm, two paw cubes and a toe), all swinging as one rigid unit; the three body blocks, the three head blocks and the four back spines never move.

The tail sweeps side to side (HydroliscModel.java:342-352): the cosine of the age x 1.0 x 0.65, x pi x 0.15, taken at a quarter, a half and three quarters along the three segments, each next segment's position re-derived 5 and 8 units along the previous segment's yaw (an FK chain written by hand on flat bones: when this rig lands, a keyframed sweep must either key the positions too or the tail bones must be parented). While the pet sits (isInSittingPose, :343-345) the sweep is zeroed - the ONLY visible sitting pose the code has; the legs and body do not change.

The crest reads the pet's health (HydroliscModel.java:353-357): the health fraction multiplies both the rate and the amplitude of the three feathers - the outer pair mirror each other around +-0.9 rad (52 deg) at 0.75 x 0.65 x hf, the centre feather wags at 1.25 x 0.65 x hf, each pi x 0.2 x hf. At full health a 36-degree fan every 12.9 (outer) and 7.7 (centre) ticks; near death almost still.
The head does not turn: netHeadYaw and headPitch are unused, so the LookAtPlayerGoal and RandomLookAroundGoal (EntityHydrolisc.java:73, 75) move nothing visible.
In water it bobs upward every tick (EntityHydrolisc.java:102-105) with the FloatGoal at the surface (:67); the renderer halves the scale for a baby (HydroliscRenderer.java:37-41).
